h: Turning Cromer Into a Two-Part Day
p: Here's the beauty of having a tropical zoo in a seaside town: you never have to choose between animals and the beach. Amazona sits on the southern side of Cromer, so it's an easy hop back into the middle of town once you've done the rounds, and a couple of hours is plenty to see everything without rushing.

Once you're back in town, the pier is the obvious next stop. It's one of the few in the country still home to a proper end-of-the-pier theatre, the Pavilion, and a wander out over the waves is free and blowy in the best way. Near the pier, the RNLI Henry Blogg Museum tells the story of Cromer's most famous lifeboatman, whose rescues earned him more medals than any other lifeboat crew member, and it's a gripping one for older children. Then there's the crab. Cromer crab is the town's calling card, and a fresh crab sandwich on the front is a bit of a rite of passage.

Fancy stretching your legs? Felbrigg Hall, a National Trust estate with woods and parkland, is just a few miles west, and the North Norfolk Railway runs heritage steam trains between Sheringham and Holt, so you can easily build a long weekend out of this stretch of coast.

Little tip: the zoo is uphill from the beach, so if you're walking from the seafront with toddlers, the car or a buggy will save some moans. Parking in the middle of Cromer can be tight on sunny summer days, so leaving the car near the zoo and strolling down into town is often the easier option.
